The Log-Tail Route of the CDF Derivatives

Source: R/log_tail.R
log_tail_route.Rd

The function is called from the bodies of distrib_grad_cdf(), distrib_hess_cdf(), distrib_deriv3_cdf() and distrib_deriv4_cdf() before dispatch. On the log scale it returns the derivatives of \(\log P\), where \(P\) is the requested tail, from ls_log_tail_derivs() for the eight location-scale families listed in log_tail_ls, and from quad_log_tail_derivs() for the families listed in log_tail_quad (and, for the lower tail, log_tail_quad_lower) at the quantiles where \(\log P\) is below log_tail_cut; the other quantiles go to the family's own method. Elsewhere it returns NULL and the generic dispatches as usual.

log_tail_ls maps each location-scale class to its base and to the map \(w\) of its second parameter; log_tail_quad lists the classes of the quadrature route for both tails and log_tail_quad_lower those for the lower tail, which adds the two Weibull families; log_tail_cut is the threshold, \(-5\); log_tail_off holds the switch that turns the route off while quantiles are sent back to the family's method.

The quantiles are selected on tail_cdf(), the value that the family's method computes first. While the method runs on the quantiles that are not far, log_tail_stash holds that value with the class, quantiles, parameters and tail to which it belongs, and tail_cdf() returns it for a call with the same arguments instead of evaluating the distribution function again. A parameter of length one is passed to the method as a scalar.

Usage

log_tail_route(distrib, q, theta, order, lower.tail, log, generic)

Arguments

distrib

An object inheriting from distrib.

q

A numeric vector of quantiles, already recycled by the generic.

theta

A named list of parameters, already aligned by the generic.

order

The derivative order, 1 to 4.

lower.tail

A single logical; TRUE selects the lower tail and FALSE the upper tail.

log

A single logical; TRUE selects the derivatives of the log probability and FALSE those of the probability.

generic

The generic of that order, called back on the quantiles that stay with the family's method: those that are not far, and those whose tail reaches outside the double range, which quad_log_tail_derivs() marks.

Value

A named list of numeric vectors, keyed as deriv_names(distrib@params, order) (in the order of hess_names() at order two), or NULL.

Examples

d <- gaussian1_distrib()
# This is log S = log(1 - Phi(z)) at z = 40, where 1 - Phi(z) underflows.
distributions7:::log_tail_route(d, 40, list(mu = 0, sigma = 1), 1L,
                                FALSE, TRUE, distrib_grad_cdf)
#> $mu
#> [1] 40.02497
#> 
#> $sigma
#> [1] 1600.999
#>
